personas.name: Reviewer
personas.role: Reviews a brief before any of its rows is dispatched

stories.text: As the reviewer, I want the secrets broker's implementation brief in the design-system form, with numbered requirements and criteria, so that its rows can be reviewed and dispatched one at a time.

personas.name: Person
personas.role: Grants an agent provisioned under them access to an account

stories.text: As a person granting an agent access, I want to give it a handle under my own grant, limited by uses, time and spend, so that it can use the account without ever holding the credential and the grant traces back to me.
As a person, I want to drop an agent's handle and have every new call on it refused at once, so that taking access back does not wait on rotating the real key.

personas.name: AI Agent
personas.role: Uses a handle for its outbound calls and reads its sealed records

stories.text: As an agent, I want to make my call with my handle and have the proxy swap in the credential, refreshing an expired OAuth token itself, so that I can do my work without ever seeing a credential.
As an agent, I want to ask for one of my sealed memories by name and get back only the piece I am permitted, so that a secret never sits in plain text in my memory files.

personas.name: Token revolver
personas.role: The worker that runs Claude sessions and builders and turns to the next account on usage-limit words

stories.text: As the token revolver, when a session prints its usage-limit words, I want to ask the broker for my next account instead of walking my own list, so that the spread across accounts is the broker's and no pool file is copied to my machine.

personas.name: Engine
personas.role: Whichever runtime starts and ends a seat

stories.text: As the engine starting a seat, I want the door to give me the seat's own login from the store at spawn and record which token went to which seat, so that I read no pool file when the broker is there and still work from my own when it is not.

personas.name: Operator
personas.role: Keeps the accounts and revokes access

stories.text: As an operator, I want to rest an account by one change in the store, so that no worker gives it another call and no file is copied to any machine.

As an operator revoking access, I want each case to say what it reaches: a handle refuses new calls, a call already admitted follows the stated cancellation rule, a login token's seat is ended by its engine, and read knowledge stays read, so that I am never told revocation took back what it cannot.

personas.name: Reviewer
personas.role: Reads the audit of what the broker did

stories.text: As a reviewer reading the audit, I want one line per use naming the seat, the handle, the real account and the time, and one per sealed read, so that every use is attributed to an identity in one place.
As a reviewer reading the audit, I want each call that was in flight when its handle was dropped to show the outcome the cancellation rule gave it, so that no call's end is unaccounted for.

personas.name: Account holder
personas.role: Uses and deliberately delegates scoped access without exposing credentials

stories.text: As a person allowed to use an account, I want the screen and server to distinguish that from permission to lend it, so I cannot accidentally grant my agent authority I do not hold.
As Dana, I want my private secrets and their metadata isolated from Tom and his agents unless I grant access, so knowing an identifier or signing in to the same installation does not disclose them.
As a person reviewing a grant or revocation, I want its source, selected service account and confirmed or unconfirmed outcome shown, so I know exactly what authority changed.

personas.name: Lead
personas.role: Reviews SECRETS-003's rows before any is dispatched

stories.text: As the lead, I want the revolver's call site, the pool file's consumers, every credential path into a seat and what the lys formats can carry recorded from source by file and line, so that the contract rests on what the code does today rather than on memory.
As the lead, I want the broker's contract and an adversarial review by someone other than its author before any code, so that every named attack has a clause defeating it before it can be built in.

personas.name: Implementer
personas.role: Is dispatched one SECRETS-003 code row at a time

stories.text: As the implementer of a code row, I want the row to name the SECRETS-002 requirements it delivers, its counted legs, its hours and what blocks it, so that I build from one row and nothing is described twice.

personas.name: Person
personas.role: Keeps credentials with the standalone identity platform

stories.text: As a person keeping credentials, I want the broker to come with Lys alone, so that I never have to install Cambium to keep a credential.
